headline: Growth continues, one-off safety charge dents GAAP margins
summary_short: ResMed's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue rose 8.6% y/y to $1,464M and non-GAAP diluted EPS grew 16% to $2.95, but a $42M Astral field-safety charge cut GAAP gross margin 200bps y/y and held GAAP diluted EPS growth to just 2% ($2.64).
summary_long: Revenue grew 8.6% y/y (9% as reported, 8% constant-currency) on broad-based demand across sleep devices, masks and software; Americas Sleep and Breathing revenue grew 8%, Rest of World grew 10% (constant currency). Non-GAAP diluted EPS rose 16% to $2.95 on sales growth and 90bps of non-GAAP gross-margin expansion from productivity gains. GAAP gross margin fell 200bps to 58.8%, driven entirely by a $42M Astral field-safety-notification charge; GAAP diluted EPS grew only 2% to $2.64 as a result. Free cash flow fell 20.6% y/y to $404M. The board raised the quarterly dividend 10% to $0.66/share and guided FY2027 shareholder capital returns above $1.85B, up from FY2026's $1.0B (+70%). ResMed also agreed to sell MatrixCare, expected to close in Q1 FY2027.

CEO Mick Farrell cited "continued momentum of our global business" and record capital returns, alongside 9% revenue growth and a 16% non-GAAP EPS increase.
